relevance.rationale: Analyses several gedanken experiments testing black hole complementarity and concludes it cannot be ruled out on known physical principles: experiments designed by an outside observer to disprove a quantum-mechanical stretched horizon require Planck-scale knowledge, and an observer who falls in after sampling the Hawking radiation cannot find the duplicate information inside before hitting the singularity. rem:information-paradox-incompleteness adopts precisely the complementarity-adjacent position — 'sections exist behind the horizon but no finite braid computation from outside produces them' — and defends it with a Goedel analogy while citing only hawking1975, goedel1931, bekenstein1973, thooft2016 and harlow-ooguri2021. The operational no-duplication argument here is the standard physical support for that position and is missing from the block. Supporting rather than core: it is context for an interpretive block, and no corpus derivation depends on it. Note this file is byte-identical (md5 74615d20...) to library/arxiv-hep-th-9308100v1/9308100v1.pdf, so the same document sits in the upload directory twice.

keyResults.statement: An observer who samples the Hawking radiation and then crosses the horizon cannot discover the duplicated information inside the black hole before reaching the singularity, so no single observer detects a violation of quantum xeroxing.
keyResults.useForFolio: The operational argument for 'information preserved but inaccessible', the position rem:information-paradox-incompleteness adopts by assertion; citing it converts an unsupported stance into a sourced one.

proposedActions.rationale: rem:information-paradox-incompleteness selects one of three positions on the paradox with no citation for the choice; the no-duplication gedanken argument is the standard support.

relevance.rationale: Susskind-Thorlacius 1993 gedanken-experiment paper arguing that black hole complementarity cannot be ruled out by known physics: experiments designed to disprove a quantum-mechanical stretched horizon need Planck-scale input, infalling observers cannot see duplicated information before the singularity, and baryon-number-violation probes give effects well outside the stretched horizon. The corpus's black-hole content (rem-level blocks in information-theory: information-paradox-incompleteness, incompleteness-horizon, hawking-radiation, plus the fluid-dynamics acoustic-horizon blocks) reframes the paradox as arithmetic incompleteness -- the horizon as a syntax boundary in Gamma(S, A_0), Bekenstein-Hawking entropy counting degree-1 witnesses -- and cites hawking1975, bekenstein1973, goedel1931. 'Complementarity' does not appear anywhere in the corpus. No result of this paper is consumed.
